## Mid Atlantic Social and Cultural

Indicators: Commercial port activity, recreational fishery engagement, social vulnerability

:::: {.soe-50-50-slide}

::: {.soe-50-column}

```{r commercial-engagement}
return_plot("commercial-engagement", region = "MidAtlantic", mode = "slide")
```

:::

::: {.soe-50-column}


```{r recreational-engagement, fig.alt= "Recreational engagement and population relative engagement with labels for the top recreationally engaged fishing communities in the Mid-Atlantic."}
return_plot("recreational-engagement", region = "MidAtlantic", mode = "slide")
```

- More variability in the most commercially active ports (based on dealers, landings, and permits) -- Cape May and Reedville
- Increasing activity in Shinnecock/Hampton Bays
- Crew Survey shows inconsistent job satisfaction and aging of the fleet
- Highly fishing-engaged communities with med-high to high census-derived vulnerability indicators: Bronx, NY, Hampton Bays/Shinnecock, NY, Newport News, VA, Morehead City, NC

:::

## Mid Atlantic Social and Cultural

Indicators: Commercial fishery revenue climate vulnerability

:::: {.soe-50-50-slide}

::: {.soe-50-column}

```{r commvulex}
return_plot("commvulex", region = "MidAtlantic", mode = "slide")
```

- Measures of how dependent communities are on species sensitive to environmental variability (temperature, acidifcation, etc.)
- Many communities, especially those in the Chesapeake Bay, are dependent on species that are _very highly sensitive_ to environmental variability
- On average, Mid Atlantic communities' landings are composed of species that are _moderately sensitive_ to environmental variability, while community revenue is derived from species that are _highly sensitive_ to environmental variability. 

:::
